message.text: How does Safari on Vision Pro deliver WebXR input? I need to know which input-source indices our select handlers in web/input/xr.js should listen on, whether enabling hand tracking changes them, and what three.js r170 does about it. Cite the sources.

I remember Apple introduced a "transient-pointer" target ray mode: the input source only exists while the user pinches, and its ray starts from the eyes at selectstart. I should verify that on webkit.org and in the WebXR spec, then check how three.js's WebXRManager assigns controller indices to input sources that come and go, and finally compare with Quest for the fallback path.

message.text:
# Introducing Natural Input for WebXR in Apple Vision Pro

visionOS exposes a new XRTargetRayMode, "transient-pointer". When the person pinches, an XRInputSource is added to the session and a selectstart event fires; the targetRaySpace of that source is positioned on the line of sight at the moment of the pinch and then follows the motion of the hand for as long as the pinch is held. When the fingers release, select and selectend fire and the input source is removed. Because the source exists only during the gesture, pages must handle inputsourceschange and must not assume a fixed set of controllers. Hand tracking ("hand-tracking" optional feature) is available behind a permission prompt and provides joint poses only; it never fires select events itself.
message.summary: → transient-pointer: source appears at selectstart, follows the hand, removed after selectend

message.text: That settles the index question. Slots are assigned first-free, and a new input source is dropped when every existing controller already has one. With hand tracking granted, the two persistent hand input sources arrive at session start and occupy slots 0 and 1, so the transient pinch pointers land on 2 and 3. Without hand tracking, pinches land on 0 and 1. And since getController(i) is what creates a slot, any index we did not request before the session started simply never receives the pinch. Create 0..3 up front, or listen on the XRSession directly. Now the Quest side, for the fallback path.

message.text:
# Hand Tracking in WebXR (Meta Horizon)

Add "hand-tracking" to optionalFeatures when requesting the session. When the person sets the controllers down, Browser swaps the input sources: the two controller sources are removed and two hand sources are added (targetRayMode "tracked-pointer", handedness left/right, inputSource.hand holding 25 XRJointSpaces). Pinch gestures on hands fire selectstart/select/selectend on the same input source, so a page that listens on controllers 0 and 1 keeps working across the swap. Hand meshes are the page's responsibility; Browser only provides joint poses. Passthrough (immersive-ar) is supported alongside hand tracking.

message.text:
XRInputSource.targetRayMode — values

"gaze": the target ray originates at the viewer's eyes and follows the direction they are facing.
"screen": the target ray originates from a touch on a 2D screen (handheld AR).
"tracked-pointer": the target ray comes from a tracked controller or hand.
"transient-pointer": the input source is created for a single interaction (for example a pinch on visionOS); the ray is valid from selectstart to selectend and the source is removed afterwards.

Browser compatibility: transient-pointer — Safari on visionOS 2+.

Here is what the sources say, and what it means for `web/input/xr.js`.

1. **visionOS Safari exposes a pinch as a transient input source.** Its `targetRayMode` is `"transient-pointer"`; the source is added right before `selectstart`, its `targetRaySpace` starts on the line of sight at that instant and then follows the hand while the pinch is held, and it is removed right after `selectend` (WebKit blog; WebXR spec; MDN).
2. **three.js r170 assigns each new input source to the first free controller slot** (`WebXRManager.onInputSourcesChange`). Without hand tracking a pinch arrives on index 0 (a second simultaneous pinch on 1). With `hand-tracking` granted, the two persistent hand sources take 0 and 1 at session start, so the transient pointers appear on **2 and 3**.
3. **Slots exist only if you asked for them.** `renderer.xr.getController(i)` creates the slot; a source that finds no free slot is ignored. So create controllers 0..3 *before* `requestSession`, listen on all four, and also listen on the `XRSession` itself (`selectstart`/`select`/`selectend`) and resolve the ray with `frame.getPose(inputSource.targetRaySpace, refSpace)`.
4. **Do not request `hand-tracking` on Vision Pro by default.** It adds an in-session permission prompt and only shifts the indices; hands never fire select themselves. Quest is different: hands and controllers swap on the same two tracked-pointer sources and pinches fire select there too (Meta docs).

Rule for us: on Vision Pro the select ray at `selectstart` is the targeting truth (it is the eye gaze); the head ray is cosmetic.

| device | hand-tracking | pinch / trigger index |
|---|---|---|
| Vision Pro | off | 0 (second pinch 1) |
| Vision Pro | on | 2, 3 |
| Quest 3S | hands or controllers | 0, 1 |

Sources: https://webkit.org/blog/15162/introducing-natural-input-for-webxr-in-apple-vision-pro/ · https://www.w3.org/TR/webxr/#dom-xrtargetraymode-transient-pointer · https://github.com/mrdoob/three.js/blob/r170/src/renderers/webxr/WebXRManager.js · https://developers.meta.com/horizon/documentation/web/webxr-hands/

message.text: Does the ray keep updating while the pinch is held? We need that for carry-at-distance when piping a tile.
message.summary: Does the ray keep updating while the pinch is held?

message.text: The WebKit post said the ray follows the motion of the hand for as long as the pinch is held, so yes. Worth stating how to read it per frame and the one caveat: the origin starts at the eyes, not at the hand.
message.summary: The WebKit post said the ray follows the motion of the hand for as long as the pinch is held, so ye…

message.text: Yes. While the pinch is held the transient pointer's `targetRaySpace` follows the hand, so you can read `frame.getPose(inputSource.targetRaySpace, refSpace)` every frame between `selectstart` and `selectend`. The caveat for carry-at-distance: the initial ray starts at the eyes, so keep the hit distance from `selectstart` and apply only the ray's change to the carried tile; do not re-origin it at the hand.
message.summary: Yes.

Bug 275318 – [visionOS] MediaStreamTrack from getUserMedia reports muted after requestSession("immersive-vr")

Status: NEW. Reported against visionOS 2 beta 4. Steps: acquire an audio track on the 2D page, enter immersive-vr, observe track.muted === true until the session ends. One later comment reports the track staying live on a newer build but with the AudioContext suspended until resumed from a gesture. No confirmation from WebKit engineers in the thread.

message.text: Unverified, and I would not build on it. There is an open WebKit report of the audio track going muted on entering immersive-vr (filed against a visionOS 2 beta) and one later comment saying it stays live if the AudioContext is resumed from a gesture; nothing authoritative either way. Plan: acquire the mic and create the AudioContext inside the ENTER button handler on the 2D page, keep the stream alive, and if `track.muted` flips or the track ends at session start, switch to "headset looks, laptop speaks" and say so in the narration. Test it in the first Vision Pro slot, not the last.
